stem: Draw the straight line $y + 3 = 2x$. Any two points on the line will do; the equation under the graph updates as you drag.
solution: Get $y$ on its own: subtract $3$ from both sides, so $y = 2x - 3$. The $3$ changes sign when it crosses the equals sign.
Read $y = mx + c$: the gradient is $m = 2$ and the $y$-intercept is $c = -3$.
Drag the first point onto the $y$-intercept, $(0, -3)$.
Use the gradient: $m = 2$ means up 2 for every 1 across, so the second point is $(1, -1)$.
Check the live equation reads $y = 2x - 3$, which is the same line as $y + 3 = 2x$.
notes: Draws the book's ex6-2-5 theme in reverse (equation to graph). Reading the printed '+3' as the intercept gives y = 2x + 3: slope right, intercept wrong, so intercept-wrong is a clean signature of the moved-term sign error. Off-target is mapped to the swap (y = 3x + 2 or y = -3x + 2) because the other named errors fire intercept-wrong here; off-target is a residual predicate, so this mapping is the weakest of the three. The slope is 2, an integer within the |m| <= 5 limit, and the intercept -3 is within -5..5.
